title: EDPB and DPAs from countries and organisation with EU adequacy decision take stock of progress and set 2027 priorities
summary: Brussels, 19 November - The EDPB met on 17 November with Commissioners and representatives of the Data Protection Authorities (DPAs) from the countries and the international organisation with an EU adequacy decision. This gathering marked the third of its kind, following the first one in October 2024 and the second one in December 2025 . The meeting was an opportunity to discuss the joint activities carried out in 2026 and identify the way forward for 2027. “The authorities in this network are essential partners for the EDPB: together we can advance privacy and data protection on a global scale. The engagement at this meeting reflects our collective commitment to addressing today's most pressing data protection challenges. With technology operating on a global scale, we must work together to address the shared issues we face in different parts of the world. I look forward to continuing and strengthening our cooperation.” EDPB Chair, Anu Talus Focus for 2027 The network has identified two priority topics for knowledge-sharing in 2027: Wearable devices with a special focus on smart glasses Privacy preserving age assurance The participants also agreed to continue discussing enforcement cooperation. Background An adequacy decision is a key-mechanism in EU data protection legislation which allows free flow of personal data from Europe to third countries or an international organisation offering an adequate level of data protection.* To date, the following countries and international organisation benefit from this: Andorra, Argentina, Brazil, Canada, Faroe Islands, Guernsey, Isra

title: Norwegian DPA fines private individual for credit check and publication of personal data without a lawful basis
summary: Background information Date of final decision: 16/10/2026 National case Controller: Private individual Legal References: Article 6(1) (Lawfulness of processing) Decision: Administrative fine Key words: Legal basis, Fines, GDPR enforcement, Basic principles Summary of the Decision Origin of the case The Data Protection Authority received a complaint from an individual who had been subject to a credit check carried out by a private individual. The individual had access to a credit information service through their work and had used it to carry out a credit check on the complainant for personal purposes. The information obtained from the credit check was subsequently published in various Facebook groups. Key Findings The Data Protection Authority concluded that the credit check was carried out for personal purposes and was unrelated to the work of the individual concerned. The Data Protection Authority therefore concluded that neither the credit check nor the subsequent publication of the information had a lawful basis under Article 6(1) of the GDPR. Decision The Data Protection Authority issued a decision imposing an administrative fine of EUR 940 on the individual for carrying out an unlawful credit check and publishing the information. For further information: Norwegian Press Release: Gebyr for kredittvurdering og publisering av personopplysningar utan rettsleg grunnlag English Press Release: Fine for credit check and publication of personal data without a lawful basis

title: Italian DPA fines Meta EUR 805 million for unlawful access to Facebook users’ photo galleries
summary: Background information Date of final decision: 13/11/2026 National case Controller: Meta Platforms Ireland Limited Decision: Administrative fine, Compliance order Key words: Fines, Online platforms Summary of the Decision Origin of the case The Italian Data Protection Authority (DPA) launched an investigation following a complaint submitted in July 2025 by the Bolzano Consumer Protection Centre concerning Facebook's access to users' smartphone photo galleries. The investigation focused on the feature “Get suggestions from your gallery while browsing Facebook”, which displays photos and videos stored on Android devices as suggestions for sharing on the social network. The Authority carried out a technical analysis of the feature and examined whether Meta had obtained valid consent and adequately informed users before accessing information stored on their devices. Key Findings The investigation found that Facebook requested a single system permission to access photos and videos for several different functions. The request was preceded by a generic notice referring to enabling other features, without clearly explaining that access would also enable gallery suggestions. The feature was enabled by default, although it could operate only after system permission had been granted. Once authorised, the app could access the device's multimedia archive on an ongoing basis. The DPA found that Meta had not obtained specific, informed consent for this feature, in breach of Article 122 of the Italian Data Protection Code. title: Italian DPA fines a company EUR 25 500 over employee access rights and corporate email accounts
summary: Background information Date of final decision: 20/10/2026 National case Controller: Techpartner S.r.l. Legal References: Article 5 (Principles relating to processing of personal data), Article 12 (Transparent information, communication and modalities for the exercise of the rights of the data subject), Article 15 (Right to access by the data subject),  Decision: Administrative fine, Compliance order Key words: Fines, Basic principles, Data subjects rights Summary of the Decision Origin of the case The Italian Data Protection Authority (DPA) received a complaint from a former employee of Techpartner concerning an inadequate response to a request to access personal data processed during employment. The DPA also examined the company's internal policies governing employees' individual corporate email accounts, including their management after employment ended. Key Findings The company did not respond to the former employee's access request within the deadline required by the GDPR. The company replied only after the DPA opened its investigation, approximately nine months after the request. Its internal rules also allowed former employees' email accounts to remain active for three to six months after termination, with the possibility of reading incoming messages. The DPA found this incompatible with the principles of lawfulness, data minimisation and storage limitation. It confirmed infringements of Articles 5(1)(a), (c) and (e), 12(3) and 15 GDPR. Other allegations concerning video surveillance and occupational medical information did not result in established infringements

This own-volition Inquiry was launched by the DPC in January 2020, in its role as the Lead Supervisory Authority for MTCH. This decision concerns MTCH’s failure to provide Tinder users with a complete copy of their personal data on request, pursuant to Article 15(3) GDPR. In particular, the DPC assessed the operation of a self-service tool on Tinder (known as the Download My Data tool), which enabled users to download their data. Although this tool was presented to users as a way to obtain a copy of their Tinder data, the DPC found that it failed to provide users with all of their personal data. Certain categories of information were omitted without notice to the user, or provided in summary form only. The DPC also found that the personal data provided through the tool did not meet the requirements of the right of access under the GDPR. title: EDPB supports use of other models of contractual clauses for onward transfers of personal data
summary: Brussels 13 November – At its latest plenary, the EDPB adopted a statement on the use of other models of contractual clauses for onward transfers of personal data * . The statement welcomes recent updates made by the European Commission on its FAQs on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) **, recognising that the Model Contractual Clauses (MCCs) developed by the Council of Europe (CoE MCC) and the ones developed by the Ibero-American Data Protection Network (RIPD MCC) may also be used for onward transfers of personal data received under the EU SCCs. Result of a joint work The EDPB and the Commission cooperated closely on this matter. The Board welcomes the Commission’s recognition of these additional instruments to onward transfer personal data received under the EU SCCs. This means that, under the conditions explained in the Commission’s FAQs, an appropriate level of protection of individuals as guaranteed by the European data protection law may be provided when data is onward transferred on the basis of these sets of clauses. In addition, the EDPB statement provides practical guidance to organisations seeking to rely on these MCCs, subject to the conditions set out in the Commission’s FAQs. Note to editors: * Model contractual clauses are contractual clauses developed by organisations and third countries. summary: Bruxelles, 11 novembre – Nel corso dell’ultima sessione plenaria, il CEPD ha adottato una dichiarazione sul primo riesame del funzionamento della decisione di adeguatezza relativa alla Repubblica di Corea e la versione definitiva delle raccomandazioni sulla richiesta di approvazione e sugli elementi e principi che figurano nelle norme vincolanti d’impresa per responsabili del trattamento (BCR-P) . Inoltre, il Comitato ha selezionato il tema della sua sesta azione coordinata di applicazione (MCE). La dichiarazione del CEPD sul primo riesame della decisione di adeguatezza relativa alla Repubblica di Corea si concentra principalmente sulla valutazione delle modifiche apportate al quadro giuridico coreano in materia di protezione dei dati, sia per quanto riguarda gli aspetti commerciali sia per quanto riguarda l’accesso ai dati personali e il loro utilizzo da parte delle autorità pubbliche coreane*. «Il riconoscimento reciproco di norme equivalenti in materia di protezione dei dati tra l’UE e la Repubblica di Corea nel 2025 ha rappresentato un passo importante, che conferma il crescente allineamento tra i due quadri normativi. Accogliamo con favore le modifiche apportate alla legislazione coreana in materia di protezione dei dati, che hanno rafforzato il livello di protezione delle persone fisiche e agevolato il trattamento dei dati da parte dei titolari del trattamento, mantenendo al contempo un livello di protezione sostanzialmente equivalente a quello previsto dal RGPD.» Anu Talus, presidente del CEPD Ad esempio, la legge sulla protezione delle informazioni personali (PIPA)

Key Findings The Italian DPA found serious shortcomings in the technical and organisational measures implemented by Wind Tre to ensure the security of personal data. title: Italian DPA fines Poste Italiane and Deutsche Bank a combined EUR 81 000 for lack of transparency in personal data processing
summary: Summary of the Decision Origin of the case The Italian Data Protection Authority (DPA) received a complaint from an employee of Poste Italiane who, following the rejection of a loan application submitted through BancoPosta, discovered that information concerning her financial situation was accessible through a platform used by authorised company staff. The information included her net income and existing financial commitments. The complainant questioned the disclosure of these data and requested their erasure. The DPA launched an investigation into the processing of personal data by Poste Italiane and Deutsche Bank in connection with the promotion and provision of BancoPosta loans. Key Findings The investigation established that, contrary to their contractual arrangements, Poste Italiane and Deutsche Bank acted as independent data controllers. Poste Italiane collected loan applications and carried out intermediary activities, including identifying financial products suited to applicants' needs, while Deutsche Bank independently assessed creditworthiness and decided whether to grant the loans. The DPA found that the privacy notices provided by both companies did not adequately reflect their respective roles and the personal data exchanged between them. In particular, Poste Italiane had failed to provide sufficiently clear information on the processing carried out during the promotion and distribution of loans, including the recipients of personal data and information flows involving the bank. title: EDPB helps kids stay safe online
summary: Brussels, 04 November - European Data Protection Authorities (DPAs) work together to protect personal data, especially for children who are more vulnerable online. Kids may not recognise risks easily, trust strangers, or share personal data carelessly. Many apps collect their data, and without proper safeguards, they could be exposed to harmful content and leave long-lasting digital footprints. This is why the EDPB launches ‘Privacy for Kids’ , a new hub for parents, teachers, and educators. It provides engaging and children friendly resources such as games, videos and quizzes, to understand online privacy. Eddy the beaver and his friends will guide you through materials from DPAs from all over Europe , available in different languages. An intuitive filtering system helps you find educational resources by selecting from: Age groups: 3-10, 11-15, and 16+. Geographic coverage: all 27 EU Member States plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway Topics: sharing online, social media, smartphones and apps, privacy at home, privacy at school, cyberbullying, smart toys, etc. Content formats: projects, informational campaigns, games, infographics, videos, quizzes, and more. title: Norwegian DPA fines Xandr EUR 8 600 000 for unlawful processing of personal data
summary: Background information Date of final decision: 2 October 2026 National case  Controller: Xandr Inc. Legal References: Article 6 (Lawfulness of processing), Article 9 (Processing of special categories of personal data) Decision: Administrative fine Key words: Fines, Basic principles, Marketing, Online platforms Summary of the Decision Origin of the case   The case started in 2020 when the Norwegian Consumer Council lodged a complaint against the advertising technology company Xandr (at the time AppNexus, now a part of Microsoft) with the Norwegian DPA (Data Protection Authority). The case concerns real-time bidding in Grindr, a location-based dating app aimed at gay, bi, trans and queer people. Key Findings  The Norwegian DPA has found it proven by clear preponderance of probability that Xandr processed Grindr users’ personal data, at least the fact that individuals were using Grindr, their advertising ID and IP addresses, during real-time bidding. These are personal data under Article 4(1) GDPR and data concerning sexual orientation under Article 9(1) GDPR. Xandr is considered a joint controller for the processing, both as supply-side and demand-side platform. Since the data were special category personal data, explicit consent under Article 9(2)(a) was the relevant legal basis for the processing. Xandr did not obtain consent itself, but relied on Grindr’s consent, which were invalid under Articles 4(11) and 7 GDPR. title: L'EDPB pubblica una dichiarazione sulle sfide in materia di protezione dei dati degli occhiali intelligenti
summary: Bruxelles, 13 ottobre – Durante la sua ultima plenaria, l'EDPB ha adottato una dichiarazione sugli occhiali intelligenti e ha pubblicato la relazione dal titolo "The connected gaze. Registrazione video, sorveglianza e somministrazione di prove nell'era degli occhiali intelligenti" *, sviluppato nel contesto del programma del gruppo di sostegno di esperti (SPE) **. Man mano che gli occhiali intelligenti diventano ampiamente disponibili e più frequentemente utilizzati, sollevano questioni significative per la protezione dei dati personali e dei diritti e delle libertà delle persone, anche se creano nuove opportunità di comunicazione, assistenza e innovazione. "Questi dispositivi sembrano normali occhiali, ma includono telecamere e microfoni e sono collegati a Internet. Ciò solleva gravi preoccupazioni in materia di privacy, in quanto le persone possono essere registrate a loro insaputa. I rischi sono ancora maggiori in ambienti sensibili, come ospedali, scuole o luoghi di lavoro, e quando le registrazioni sono condivise sui social network. E, naturalmente, i bambini sono particolarmente a rischio quando usano questi occhiali o quando vengono filmati." Presidente dell'EDPB, Anu Talus Il testo dell'EDPB è una dichiarazione iniziale che fornisce orientamenti preliminari agli utenti, ai fabbricanti e ai fornitori di servizi, aumentando nel contempo la consapevolezza dei rischi che tali dispositivi comportano. title: Italian DPA fines Emirates EUR 180 000 for infringements concerning passengers’ health data
summary: Background information Date of final decision: 14 May 2026 National case Controller: Emirates Legal Reference(s): Article 5 (Principles relating to processing of personal data), Article 12 (Transparent information, communication and modalities for the exercise of the rights of the data subject) and Article 13 (Information to be provided where personal data are collected from the data subject) Decision: Administrative fine, Compliance order Key words: Health and research, Basic principles Summary of the Decision Origin of the case   The Italian Data Protection Authority (DPA) initiated an investigation following a complaint lodged by a passenger concerning the processing of health data by Emirates in connection with assistance for passengers with disabilities or reduced mobility. The complainant stated that Emirates had required her to complete a MEDIF (Medical Information for Fitness to Travel or Special Assistance) form, although she claimed not to fall within the categories of passengers required to do so. The form collected information concerning passengers’ health, as well as data relating to their doctor and any accompanying person. The complainant also raised concerns about the information provided regarding the processing of such data. Key Findings After consulting the Italian Civil Aviation Authority, the Italian DPA found that the processing of health data through the MEDIF form could be lawful where necessary to ensure safe air transport and provide appropriate assistance to passengers with disabilities or reduced mobility. Therefore, it found no infringement
